items.name: The 'Getting robbed' skit
items.what: Creators film a single-take skit where they are so absorbed in their phone that they fail to notice someone stealing their bag behind them, with on-screen text revealing what distracted them.

items.name: The 'Daily GRWM loading' format
items.what: A get-ready-with-me style video that uses a loading percentage bar starting at 0% in pajamas and progressing to 100% fully dressed, set to a sped-up version of 'Windows in Brazil'.

items.name: whimsymaxxing bedazzling trend
items.what: Creators glue plastic rhinestones onto everyday items like coffee cups, skincare bottles, and phone cases, popularized by brands like Sephora and Ulta Beauty.

items.name: Performative-distress 'alarm clock' videos
items.what: Creators film exaggerated meltdowns—crying, yelling, wrestling with phones—to shut off morning alarms from apps like Erly that require completing a task to stop ringing.

items.name: The single-take, low-production lip sync
items.what: Simple one-take lip sync performances filmed in ordinary settings without production polish, such as a truck driver lip-syncing from their cab.

items.name: The absurd-rule service skit ('Smile More or Card Declined')
items.what: Deadpan skits built around invented service counter rules where breaking the rule results in a card being declined, turning everyday transactions into relatable humor.

items.name: The 'POV: [ordinary thing] in 2026' exaggeration
items.what: Creators take mundane interactions and frame them as 'POV' while pushing one detail into absurd near-future territory, delivered with straight-faced seriousness.

items.name: The 'Netflix documentary' chair-sit format
items.what: Creators sit in a chair with dramatic documentary-style music and narrate the most mundane subjects with total gravity, mimicking a Netflix documentary.

items.name: Format-first content from niche and small business accounts
items.what: Small businesses apply broad, remixable premises like 'predicting the future' to their products, achieving reach far beyond their follower base.

items.name: Visual-illusion and green-screen tricks
items.what: Green-screen techniques transform everyday tasks into magical illusions, encouraging viewers to rewatch to figure out how the trick was done.

items.name: The bait-and-switch hook
items.what: Short skits using a two-beat setup-then-twist structure, such as offering a discount before revealing an unexpected punchline.

items.name: Stylized transformations (Ghibli, anime, Pixar-style)
items.what: AI-generated videos that transform ordinary photos or moments into hand-painted or 3D-rendered scenes in styles like Ghibli, anime, or Pixar.

items.name: Template-Based AI Videos
items.what: Creators start from pre-built templates like transitions, reveals, or scene structures and swap in their own photos, clips, or products for faster, consistent content creation.

items.name: AI talking-avatar and UGC-style content
items.what: Product reviews, testimonials, and explainers delivered by consistent AI presenters, allowing brands to post daily without a person on camera.

items.name: AI Story Series & Multi-Episode Content
items.what: Creators build recurring characters across numbered episodes, aligning with a shift toward series-based content outperforming single viral posts for long-term growth.
